explanations: The emerald is a variety of beryl, coloured green by traces of chromium or vanadium, and rates 7.5 to 8 on the Mohs scale.
The ruby is corundum in pinkish-red to blood-red; some famous stones called rubies, such as the Black Prince's, are really spinels.
The sapphire is corundum in any colour but red, most familiar in blue, and at 9 on the Mohs scale is the third hardest mineral.
Emerald, ruby and sapphire are three of the traditional cardinal gems, mineral crystals cut and polished to be worn as jewellery.

sources.excerpt: Emerald is a gemstone and a variety of the mineral beryl (Be3Al2(SiO3)6) colored green by trace amounts of chromium or sometimes vanadium.
Beryl has a hardness of 7.5–8 on the Mohs scale.
It occurs mainly in association with quartz, muscovite, albite, schorl, microcline, fluorite, smoky quartz and elbaite.
Ruby is a pinkish-red to blood-red-colored gemstone, a variety of the mineral corundum, consisting of aluminium oxide (α-Al2O3).
Some gemstones that are popularly or historically called rubies, such as the Black Prince's Ruby in the British Imperial State Crown, are actually spinels.

Sapphire is a precious gemstone, a variety of the mineral corundum, consisting of aluminium oxide (α-Al2O3) with trace amounts of elements such as iron, titanium, cobalt, lead, chromium, vanadium, magnesium, boron, and silicon.
Red corundum stones also occur, but are called rubies rather than sapphires.
Sapphire has a remarkable hardness, with a score of 9 on the Mohs scale, the third-hardest mineral after diamond at 10 and moissanite at 9.5.
A gemstone (also called a fine gem, jewel, precious stone, semiprecious stone, or simply gem) is a piece of mineral crystal which, when cut or polished, is used to make jewelry or other adornments.
